artifacts.summary: 3-phase relocate-and-trim plan bringing skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md from 20930 B under its 20000 B gate-20 ceiling via two canonicality inversions and one wording tightening, then full gate close-out.

memory_candidates.content: When an eager-loaded file (a SKILL.md, a command .md) breaches its per-file context-budget ceiling and the over-budget prose is already mirrored in an on-demand architecture doc that currently defers back to it as canonical, the fix is a canonicality INVERSION rather than a deletion: expand the doc's copy to carry the full contract text, flip its closing cross-reference, and leave the eager-loaded file a short pointer. This preserves every contract statement while moving bytes out of eager context, which is exactly what the per-file ceiling exists to force. Two structural cues make a site mechanically identifiable rather than taste-based: (1) the doc's paragraph closes with a 'see <skill> for the full contract text this mirrors' deference sentence, and (2) grep confirms only those two sites claim canonicality. Verify the arithmetic by drafting the replacement text and measuring with wc -c before committing to the approach -- a single relocation often buys back less than the breach requires, and a file under chronic budget pressure (trimmed once, re-breached by the next contract addition) needs several sites plus deliberate margin, not just the one the defect report flagged.
